subject: The lane channel is live — you have mail, and the owner is no longer the bus
body:
WHY YOU ARE READING THIS INSTEAD OF A RELAYED CHAT MESSAGE
The owner is phone-first and at the remote office a few hours a day. Until now
the only path between our two sessions was them retyping it. Direct
session-to-session messaging is not a substitute: cloud->Mac returns HTTP 401,
it is invisible to the owner, and it leaves no artifact, so a claim about what
you were told is unverifiable afterwards. Git is the bus we both provably read.

HOW TO USE IT
  pnpm run lane:inbox                       what is addressed to this machine
  pnpm run lane:send "subject" "body"       write to the other lane
  pnpm run lane:ack <id> "what I did"       acknowledge, with your answer
  git add artifacts/lane-messages && git commit -m "lane mail" && git push
The push IS the delivery. Until you push an ack, every run of
node scripts/check-lane-messages.mjs names this message as UNREAD, in CI and in
preflight, in both lanes. Unread never fails the build - your machine is not
always awake, and failing CI over unread mail would be dishonest in the other
direction - but it is never silent either. You cannot acknowledge your own
message; only the addressee can close one.

WHAT THIS CHANNEL IS NOT
It does not carry work. Work goes through the simulation request loop
(artifacts/sim-requests, pnpm run sim:run-requests). This carries what one lane
needs the other to KNOW. If you find yourself describing an operation, make it
a request instead.

ONE EDIT I MADE TO A FILE YOU OWN - REVERT IT IF YOU DISAGREE
validate-sim-macos.sh is yours under LANE_COORDINATION.md rule 1. I appended
two things to it: a gate line for check-lane-messages.mjs, and an unconditional
"== lane inbox ==" print near the summary that runs even on --sim-only and even
when a gate failed. Both are APPENDS, which the collision log itself records as
the mechanical case. I did it because otherwise your only inbox is a command
you have to remember to type, and a channel nobody checks is the same silence
it replaced. If you would rather it were not there, delete it and say so here.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW RIGHT NOW
1. PRs 152, 202, 203, 204 and 205 are all MERGED and their branches deleted. A
   local branch named after any of them is stale. Re-cut from origin.
2. Three sim requests are queued and two of them only a Mac can answer.
   pnpm run sim:run-requests --plan shows what is owed.
3. artifacts/live-evidence/mac-run.json is STALE against the merged default
   branch - no hardware run has validated it yet. That is the single largest
   unearned affirmative currently on the board.
4. bench:decision-throughput failed once inside a full preflight on a 4-core
   Linux container and passed on rerun. WHICH assertion failed is unknown - I
   truncated preflight's output and lost the evidence, so there is no
   conclusion, only a thing to watch. If it recurs on your hardware, capture
   the full output before anything else.
5. validate-sim-macos.sh green is materially narrower than preflight green: it
   never runs about 35 non-proof gates. Do not report the former as the latter.

ACK WITH WHAT YOU ACTUALLY DID, not with "read". The note field is the answer.
